scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `bgpd` FRR daemon (and its supervisor `watchfrr`) on `leaf_router_0_0` has been killed and is not running, while `zebra` continues operating normally.

**Mechanism:** Without `bgpd`, `leaf_router_0_0` cannot originate or receive any BGP sessions. Both uplink interfaces (eth0 → spine_router_0_0, eth1 → spine_router_0_1) remain physically UP — which is why the NOC observed UP interfaces — but no BGP TCP session can be established without the daemon. The two spine routers each show one `Active` (retrying) BGP neighbor corresponding to `leaf_router_0_0`'s peer IPs. Because no BGP adjacency forms, `leaf_router_0_0` receives no BGP routes from the fabric. Its kernel FIB contains only three directly-connected routes (10.0.0.0/24, and the two /31 spine links); the 10.0.1.0/24 prefix (pc_0_1's subnet) is entirely absent. Every packet from pc_0_0 destined for 10.0.1.2 hits `leaf_router_0_0` (10.0.0.1) as the default gateway, finds no matching route, and is returned with ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable."

**Localization:** Solely `leaf_router_0_0` — confirmed by `pgrep` (bgpd absent), `bgp_snapshot` (ASN: none, neighbors: 0), and `ip route show` (no BGP-learned prefixes). The FRR configuration file and `daemons` file are both correct.

**Root cause:** The `bgpd` process on `leaf_router_0_0` crashed or was externally killed; because `watchfrr` was also not running, there was no automatic restart.

**Fix:** Run `service frr restart` (or `systemctl restart frr`) on `leaf_router_0_0` to bring up `bgpd` and `watchfrr`. BGP sessions to both spines will re-establish, the 10.0.1.0/24 prefix will be learned, and cross-fabric reachability will be restored immediately.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly and repeatedly identifies leaf_router_0_0 as the sole affected device.
Agent explicitly states that the bgpd FRR daemon on leaf_router_0_0 has been killed/is not running (and watchfrr is down), correctly identifying the BGP daemon as down.
